item.title: Jio IPO windfall brings mega party, early salaries, and bonus bonanza
item.description: The accelerated bonus payment brought forward a substantial portion of employees' annual performance-linked rewards ...
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: Asia's richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is known for throwing lavish weddings for his children. On Wednesday, he brought that trademark scale of celebration to a corporate milestone, hosting a mega party for thousands of employees at Reliance Corporate Park to mark the blockbuster stock market debut of Jio Platforms Ltd.The celebrations extended beyond the party: October salaries have been paid early on October 15, and 75 per cent of employees' annual cash bonus or performance-linked incentive for the 2026-27 fiscal year was disbursed on Wednesday, months ahead of the usual post-financial-year payout.Thousands of employees and their families gathered at Reliance Corporate Park in the afternoon to celebrate the listing of the digital and telecommunications business, which raised a record Rs 30,213 crore in its initial public offering and thereafter saw a bumper listing on Wednesday.Dozens of food stalls serving street food, dance performances and jam sessions blending devotional music with contemporary rhythms enthralled thousands who gathered on invitations by Ambani's scions, sources privy to the matter said.While October salary was paid a fortnight early on October 15 to enable employees bid for shares offered in the IPO, the bonus payment was brought forward to bring early Diwali, they said.The accelerated bonus payment brought forward a substantial portion of employees' annual performance-linked rewards.Akash Ambani, chairman of Reliance Jio and managing director of Jio Platforms, swapped the bandhgala and business suits he had worn for investor roadshows and the listing ceremony for a T-shirt as he addressed employees at the celebratory gala. His siblings - twin sister Isha and younger brother Anant - who had stood alongside him at key moments in the run-up to the IPO, were by his side once again.The listing marked a defining moment for Ambani's strategy to transform Reliance from an energy-focused conglomerate into a major player in telecommunications and digital services. Jio, which disrupted India's telecom market with low-cost data and voice services, has grown into a platform serving more than 540 million customers.Mukesh Ambani, who built Jio into one of India's largest telecom and digital platforms, largely ceded the spotlight to the next generation during the IPO, allowing his eldest son Akash to take the lead through investor roadshows and the listing process.While Ambani remained the architect of Reliance's larger vision, his relative absence from the public-facing campaign marked a carefully choreographed generational transition, with Akash emerging as the principal voice of Jio's ambitions before investors.His father's imprint, however, was unmistakable - in a record-breaking share sale that capped a decade of investment in building India's digital infrastructure.The festivities also extend beyond the workplace. Reliance is also organising religious ceremonies, special prayers and bhandaras - community meals offered to devotees - at prominent temples and pilgrimage centres across the country to mark Jio's listing.The planned initiatives span Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Kerala, Assam, West Bengal, Rajasthan and Odisha, combining traditional rituals with large-scale food distribution for pilgrims and local communities, they said.In Uttar Pradesh, special shringar and bhog rituals are planned at the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi, alongside a community feast for 15,000 devotees on October 29. At the Shree Annapurna Mandir, also in Varanasi, the planned feast is expected to serve 32,000 people, including 200 sadhus and sanyasis. A community lunch for 500 visitors is planned at Kanpur's Baba Anandeshwar Mandir.In Uttarakhand, food-distribution arrangements and bhandara services are planned at the Badrinath and Kedarnath temples for pilgrims and local communities. Parmarth Niketan Ashram in Rishikesh and Siddhpeeth Shri Dakshin Kali Mandir in Haridwar are also among the locations where special religious services and community meals are planned.In Mumbai, day-long community-feeding operations are planned at the Siddhivinayak, Mumba Devi, Babulnath and Mahalaxmi temples. At the Shree Mookambika Devi Mandir in Ghansoli, a 15-member bhajan group is scheduled to perform as part of a programme that includes a community feast for 5,000 devotees, sources said.The initiatives also include the Shirdi Sai Baba Temple, where festive lighting and floral decorations are planned alongside a contribution towards the temple's daily community kitchen, which serves an estimated 1,00,000 people. At Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga Mandir, the programme includes meals for 1,000 pilgrims, devotional music and offerings to 200 sadhus.In Kerala, special community meals and offerings are planned at the Sri Rajarajeswara Temple in Kannur. Other locations listed for celebrations include Kamakhya Temple in Assam, Kalighat Temple in Kolkata, Salasar Balaji Mandir in Rajasthan, Jagannath Temple in Puri and Shreenathji Temple in Nathdwara, with programmes featuring prayers, devotional music, floral decorations and community dining.The nationwide religious initiatives give the listing a distinctly Indian celebratory dimension, combining corporate milestones with traditional expressions of gratitude and community service.Jio's market debut itself was a landmark for India's equity market. The Rs 30,213-crore offering was the country's largest initial public offering, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870-crore issue in 2024.Jio shares opened at Rs 1,358, a premium of 21.4 per cent over the issue price of Rs 1,119, giving the company a strong start as a listed business.The listing marks a new chapter for Reliance's decade-long investment in building Jio into one of the world's largest telecommunications businesses, with a subscriber base exceeding 530 million and ambitions extending into cloud computing, enterprise technology and artificial intelligence.

item.title: Altman urges firms to prioritise AI security over productivity gains
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman urged companies to prioritise AI security risks over productivity gains, warning that AI systems are uncovering vulnerabilities requiring urgent action.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Technology / Artificial Intelligence / Altman urges firms to prioritise AI security over productivity gains

Altman urges firms to prioritise AI security over productivity gains OpenAI CEO Sam Altman urged companies to prioritise AI security risks over productivity gains, warning that AI systems are uncovering vulnerabilities requiring urgent action.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 29 2026 | 12:21 AM IST

Listen to This Article

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has urged companies to make understanding the security threats posed by artificial intelligence (AI) their top short-term priority, even ahead of using it to boost productivity, saying he was shocked at how many software flaws AI systems were finding.   "If I could recommend only one thing to a company right now to do with AI in the very short term, even more than become super productive with Codex (OpenAI's AI coding tool), it would be to really understand the security threat landscape from AI and mitigate against that," Altman said.   He was speaking in a conversation with Oracle CEO Clay Magouyrk at the Oracle AI World event here.

"I realise that this is probably somewhat annoying for me to say," he said, adding that it might seem like "you're creating the problem, now you're telling us we have to spend or work on the solution."   Magouyrk disagreed. "AI is not creating the problem. AI is not creating these bugs. AI is helping us discover all of the security issues that we have developed over the past 50 years," he said. Also Read

Indian startups listing younger, AI firms could follow: Accel's Swaroop premium

AI is not a bubble yet, but volatility lies ahead, says Shankar Sharma

Valuation of AI stocks, volatility pose risks for investors: Fund managers

Agreeing with the Oracle CEO, Altman noted that the only way through is to find all these issues and fix them, and that new methods would be needed because it is "too hard to patch every bug one by one across the entire supply chain that we all depend on."

He said companies would need new kinds of services that constantly monitor traffic and stop such flaws from being exploited. "I find myself shocked at just how many vulnerabilities these AI systems are finding," Altman said, adding that it would take a "herculean effort" to get ahead of the problem.   His remarks come days after a coalition of researchers and security firms led by OpenAI used AI agents to uncover serious flaws in PHP. PHP is a programming language that sits behind a majority of websites today.   On October 21, the cyber division of the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) warned that the flaws could let attackers run code remotely and advised taking websites offline if they could not be updated immediately.

Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince reported "millions" of attempts to exploit the flaws within hours of the announcement.   OpenAI called the flaws "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory" and said AI appeared to have found them before any attackers did.   OpenAI has also faced security incidents involving its own models. In July, the company said AI agents it was testing for cybersecurity capabilities had escaped their isolated test environment and broken into the systems of AI platform Hugging Face.   The models' deployment safeguards had been intentionally switched off for the test. OpenAI said at the time that "this incident   points to the need to further strengthen our model's alignment".

In September, OpenAI temporarily halted training, evaluation and tool-based use of its most capable models after an AI agent on a search task reached a public chatbot service through a gap in its internet-access restrictions.   It disclosed this in a blog post on September 25.   Altman said the pace of change in AI had been one of the biggest surprises for him this year. When OpenAI launched ChatGPT almost four years ago, its models "couldn't solve grade school math, and now they're like knocking down the hardest, unproven math problems we know of," he said.   GPT-6, OpenAI's latest model, has seen "our strongest adoption by far of any new model", he said.

AI is also letting people who never thought of themselves as programmers build their own apps, Altman pointed out. Describing his own experience of using the latest tools, he said, "It's like I am managing a factory inside of my computer, and I can get things that I don't enjoy doing to be automated

item.title: JPMorgan to lead US retail offering in Anthropic's potential record IPO
item.description: The company behind Claude has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO overall ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Ryan Gould and Shirin Ghaffary Anthropic PBC has tapped JPMorgan Chase & Co. to lead US sales of shares to individual investors in its potentially record-setting initial public offering, people familiar with the matter said. The company behind Claude has weighed a retail offering of about 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO overall, some of the people said. JPMorgan Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon is expected to take part in the Wall Street bank’s campaign, one of them added. JPMorgan is reprising its role leading the effort to gather retail orders for SpaceX’s $86.2 billion IPO, which saw more than $100 billion of demand from individual investors, Bloomberg News has reported.  Citigroup Inc. is set to coordinate the international retail offering, some of the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. Anthropic’s IPO includes offerings in Australia, Canada, Japan, certain European Economic Area countries, Switzerland and the UK, according to the IPO filing. JPMorgan is coordinating outreach on Anthropic’s IPO to high-net-worth investors and private banking clients as well as broker platforms, the people said. Deliberations are ongoing and details including the share of the offering earmarked for retail could change, the people said. Representatives for Anthropic, JPMorgan and Citigroup declined to comment. Anthropic filed publicly on Monday for an IPO that would see it and some of its investors sell shares, marking the first listing by a company focused primarily on developing the most advanced AI models. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering. Investors are telling bankers on the deal that their estimate of a fair valuation has shifted to around $1.4 trillion to $1.5 trillion, though a valuation of closer to $1.75 trillion is potentially achievable, Bloomberg News has reported. The amount of money needed to fund the development of AI and its associated infrastructure has spurred companies to raise tens of billions of dollars at a time.  Meta Platforms Inc. on Monday kicked off a plan to raise as much as $98 billion in equity, which would be one of the largest financing exercises of its kind in history. It follows Google parent Alphabet Inc.’s $85 billion equity fundraising plan earlier this year. Anthropic and rival OpenAI are seeking to raise record amounts while facing mounting public scrutiny over AI safety after a string of high-profile hacking incidents by rogue agents.

item.title: Infosys draws four downgrades in a day on weaker annual sales outlook
item.description: Brokerages turn cautious as Infosys' reduced FY27 sales guidance raises concerns over demand recovery and AI-led disruption ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Faseeh Mangi Infosys Ltd. was downgraded by at least four analysts in a single day after India’s second-largest software exporter cut its annual sales forecast, deepening concerns over disruption from artificial intelligence. Axis Capital Ltd., Arihant Capital Markets Ltd., and IIFL Capital Services Ltd. were among brokerages that lowered their ratings on Monday, data compiled by Bloomberg show. Three others reduced their recommendations over the weekend, pushing its consensus rating to 3.7 out of 5, the lowest since January 2024. The downgrades for the sector’s bellwether threatens to derail a nascent recovery in India’s battered technology shares. The Nifty IT Index is on track for its best month since July, even as concerns mount over soaring debt levels being used to fund the global AI buildout.  Infosys cutting its annual sales forecast signals that a broad-based recovery in IT budgets has yet to materialize. Revenue will rise 1% to 2% on a constant-currency basis in the year through March 2027, the company said late Friday, versus analysts’ estimates of just over 2%.  India’s $280 billion-plus software services industry has been grappling with a slowdown, with companies limiting spending in the midst of geopolitical crises such as the Iran conflict, surging energy prices and elevated inflation.  Infosys shares have fallen 28% this year on ongoing concerns about its ability to weather AI disruption. The average target price from 44 analysts is 1,200 rupees. The stock tumbled about 3% to 1,132.2 rupees in early trading on Tuesday.
